subject: Banking
title: Why Branches Still Exist
description: One-minute skill: Why Branches Still Exist.

hook.text: JPMorgan opened 400 new branches between 2018 and 2023 while everyone predicted branches would die.

buildup.text: Digital banking handles routine transactions. But mortgages, business loans.

discovery.text: Banks found that cities with branches attract more digital customers.

twist.text: The branch of 2025 looks nothing like 2005. Tellers are replaced by advisors. ATMs handle cash.

climax.text: Branches are not dying. They are evolving from transaction centers into relationship hubs for high-value decisions.

punchline.text: 400 new branches opened. Physical trust still drives digital growth.

quiz.question: Why did JPMorgan open hundreds of new branches despite digital banking growth?
options: Physical branches build trust and attract more digital customers

details.summary: Despite the digital revolution, bank branches persist because complex transactions like mortgages require human guidance, some customers lack digital access, and physical presence builds trust in communities where relationships drive business.
details.whyItMatters: Branch closure decisions affect communities and customer access. Understanding why branches persist reveals the limits of digital banking and the populations that technology still fails to serve adequately.
takeaways: Complex products like mortgages and business loans often require in-person advice
Elderly and digitally excluded populations depend on branch access
Branch closures disproportionately affect low-income and rural communities

faq.question: How many bank branches have closed in recent years?
faq.answer: US bank branches have declined from over 95,000 to under 75,000 in a decade. The UK has lost over half its branches since 2015. The trend is accelerating as digital adoption grows and cost-cutting intensifies.

faq.question: Can banking go fully digital?
faq.answer: For most customers and most transactions, yes. But advisory services for complex products, regulatory requirements for certain identity verification, and populations without smartphone access mean some physical presence will remain necessary.
